review.target_commit_context: release snapshot as published; control-layer files read 2026-11-03
review.blind_note: Controller had read v1.1 README and executive summary before designing its own independent round; the four CU first passes remained blind.
review.verdict: A-grade research memo; approximately 20% of the graded submission; model, validation, consulting narrative and Tier2 are not started

items.title: Research weight is high, model is absent
items.claim: v1.1 covers the research stage only: no model code, no solve, no figures; project_solver_run=false and control/RUN.json solver_run=false.
items.impact: Three of the five brief success criteria (modelling methodology, technical validation, consulting interpretation) are untouched.
items.ask: Compress control layer to a one-page appendix and re-centre the plan on the model this week.

items.title: Daily-chronology treatment in Tier1 blurs the Tier1/Tier2B boundary
items.claim: Brief: 'Tier 1 models should use a simplified treatment of time - detailed chronological operation of storage is not required at this stage'. v1.1 adopts a daily one-direction/one-window rule as the Tier1 core (BL-04, BL-11).
items.impact: Raises Tier1 complexity without adding accuracy and pre-consumes the Tier2B upgrade, shrinking the measurable 2B delta.
items.ask: Tier1 = aggregate-period energy balance with efficiency/capacity constraints; keep the daily rule as the 2B sub-case and a conservative sensitivity.

items.title: 107 dates with every dispatchable fuel at exactly 0 MW are not reported
items.claim: 107 dates (2022-10-17 to 2026-08-03) have nuclear/gas/coal/oil/biomass/run-of-river/pumped-storage/other all exactly 0 MW while total generation remains 1450-17614 MW.
items.impact: Under regime B, q_t = min(G_t, D_t) assigns nearly all generation to direct sale on these days, leaving nothing to charge or electrolyse: battery and H2 value under B is systematically depressed and the deficit overstated.
items.ask: Add a mandatory SA-DQ double run (all days vs 108 excluded) to the run manifest and disclose the artefact in the report.

items.title: Electrolyser CAPEX evidence routes differ by roughly 1.8x and are treated as settled
items.claim: Modern IEA route 1270-1651 GBP2020/kW_e versus legacy BEIS 672-1329 (central 816); the legacy route is demoted to sensitivity rather than presented as the decisive uncertainty.
items.impact: This spread alone can decide whether an electrolyser is built; it is the first-order sensitivity of the H2 case. The modern-case stack replacement also borrows the old BEIS absolute proxy (489.61 GBP2020/kW_e at years 11/22).
items.ask: Produce a two-way critical map (CAPEX x H2 price) with each curve labelled by source, and record 'which CAPEX route' as an open decision rather than an adopted value.

items.title: The 'simple solution from the previous consultancy' comparator is undefined
items.claim: The brief's premise is a prior consultancy proposal the client rejected, and the marking asks why the recommendation beats a simpler strategy. A0/B0 are 'no investment', not that simple solution.
items.evidence: keyword search of the whole v1.1 tree returns no 'consultancy' / 'previous solution' content
items.impact: The report cannot answer the central client question without it; this is a low-cost, high-return comparison.
items.ask: Define and quantify two comparators: (a) no investment; (b) a naive rule (e.g. 50 MW battery cycling one full window daily at the daily average price, or a static capacity estimate from annual surplus x conversion efficiency).

items.title: No decision thresholds or break-even points
items.claim: v1.1 lists scenarios to run but no thresholds; the brief calls 'what could cause the recommendation to change' a very important question.
thresholds_cu: battery arbitrage requires p_sell/p_buy > 1/0.9 = 1.111; equal-price cycling loses (1-0.9)p per MWh bought
H2 electricity-equivalent value 9.4954 GBP/kg / 55.9 kWh/kg = 169.95 GBP/MWh of input electricity
battery FOM convention moves a 3 MWh unit from 25056 to 12528 EUR2020/yr, shifting the critical capacity
items.ask: Add a 'what would change the recommendation' section driven by these three thresholds, with a tornado chart.

items.title: Discount rate and price basis are choices, but no reporting basis is fixed and ROI metrics are missing
items.claim: CDX uses 5% real in constant GBP2020; CU used 7% real in GBP2026. Neither is evidenced. The brief names ROI explicitly; no IRR/payback/ROI presentation is specified.
items.ask: Fix one reporting basis in the run manifest, report NPV x discount-rate, payback and ROI, and record the choice as a team decision.

items.title: Tier2A research is entirely absent
items.claim: No REPD pipeline, no technology-level CAPEX/LCOE, no capacity factors derived from the supplied fuel data, no connection/land costs.
items.impact: If 2A is chosen, at least a week of research is missing; if 2B is chosen, the existing temporal research is directly reusable.
items.ask: Decide Tier2 this week and record it in a message; if 2A, open a generation-side research line immediately.

items.title: Repository hygiene: duplicated first passes and an unlabelled derived CSV
items.claim: FIRST_PASS/ duplicates the topic folders; prices_gbp2020.csv (146 KB) is derived and not labelled as such.
items.ask: Add a derived-artefact note in the README and stop duplicating first passes in future versions.

classification_corrections.cdx: purchases fixed at 0, treated as closed
classification_corrections.cu: 0 is a choice, not evidence; add an adder sensitivity and report break-even a* = 0.9 p_sell - p_buy
same: label as a choice and run {0,10,20} GBP/MWh ablation
label them as decision-variable bounds, not demand estimates; 50000 kg/day implies ~116 MW continuous input
an acceptable price-elasticity threshold can bound the conclusion without half-hourly data
BEIS T&S gives 0.26-3.56 GBP/kg/100 km; enough for a stored-vs-delivered threshold
report length, appendix rules and pitch duration are directly askable; do not leave them to late November

response_request.format: reply per ID: accept / reject (with reason) / defer (with trigger)
